title: Refit a motor brush and restore its spring contact
instruction: Refit the inspected carbon brush in the open motor so its curved contact face seats on the commutator and its pressure finger rests on top. Leave both grippers clear. The motor is isolated from power; electrical reconnection is a later service step.
context: Motor repair technicians refit carbon brushes after inspecting and cleaning brush gear. A brush must slide in its close-fitting guide and remain pressed against the commutator: a brush left high or a pressure finger left off interrupts current transfer and can cause sparking when the motor returns to service. This task covers that mechanical refitting stage in an opened motor.
setup: Two YAM arms, 61 cm apart, with three RGB cameras over a 1.1 x 1.3 m wooden table. Coordinates in metres: x forward from arm bases, y left from their midpoint; heights above table. A stationary, isolated motor is bolted to a service stand: 210 mm diameter rear body, 145 mm long along y, centred (0.32,0.1125,0.105), two end-shield cheeks at x 0.205 and 0.435, bearing at (0.32,-0.112,0.105), service cover already removed. Copper commutator diameter 120 mm, length 130 mm, axis y, top at (0.32,-0.035,0.165). Brass brush box 25.2 x 32.2 mm clear opening, 3 mm walls, 30 mm high, bottom 2.5 mm above the commutator. A pre-bedded graphite brush 25 x 32 x 50 mm, 75 g, stands at (0.47,-0.12,0.00132). Steel pressure finger, 35 g, 60 mm lever, 14 mm wide, with a 30 mm downturned end; y-axis pivot at (0.26,-0.035,0.245), initially 16.09 degrees down, resting against the empty holder, passive torsion spring 0.70 N m/rad toward 80 degrees, stops -85 and 22 degrees. The disconnected flexible electrical shunt is omitted; no wire operation is scored. Both arms begin clear in the shown layout.
scoring: Terminal state: 0.25 if the brush is in its guide, tilt below 4 degrees, centre less than 1 mm from the box centre, and inserted at least 10 mm; 0.5 if also seated with no more than 0.5 mm gap at either end of its curved contact face and tilt below 1 degree; 1.0 if also the pressure finger rests on the brush top with its toe wholly over the brush, both grippers at least 5 mm clear of brush and finger, continuously for 10 steps (0.5 s). Physical checks: ruler for depth, feeler gauge for contact gap, photo for orientation and finger placement, video for release/dwell. Zero permanently for a brush outside the worktop bounds, chassis tip over 15 degrees, displaced fixed fixture, broken/detached pressure finger or other invalid shortcut. Incomplete work retains only its current valid tier; doing nothing scores zero.
reset_notes: Restore the separate brush, pressure finger angle and spring, zero all velocities and robot joints, clear scoring counters and rebuild all camera buffers. No consumables.
fidelity: Native rigid contacts, real nominal brush dimensions and 0.2 mm box clearance, curved pre-bedded face, passive torsion spring and installed motor access. Motor housing and pressure finger are representative procedural geometry, not manufacturer CAD. Electrical shunt, wiring, brush wear and powered operation are omitted; only mechanical refitting is assessed. Friction and spring load are estimates pending hardware calibration.
scores: Local prototype: not evaluated; Dream-1: not run; demo: not run
